obligations.text: Freeze overrides require an approver distinct from the requester.
Audit records are append-only and frozen once written.
Unacknowledged incidents past 15 minutes trigger SLA breach.
Rollback follows docs/runbooks/rollback.md (freeze, revert tag, verify /readyz).

planted_conflicts.description: README claims PostgreSQL/SQLite storage, while src/store/jsonStore.js uses in-memory Map storage.
ADR-0003 forbids hard deletion, while test/retention.test.js tests MemoryJsonStore.purge hard-deleting expired records.
FF_AUTO_ROLLBACK = false in src/config/flags.js is never wired into rollback or http routes.
docs/issues/018-pagerduty-sync.md plans PagerDuty sync, with no implementation.

interview_answers.question: What is HarborBoard for and who uses it?
interview_answers.answer: Release managers tracking freeze overrides, SLA breaches, and rollback readiness.

interview_answers.question: What rules must never break?
interview_answers.answer: Nobody approves their own freeze override, and audit entries are never mutated.

interview_answers.question: Which outcomes matter most?
interview_answers.answer: Zero unapproved freeze overrides and complete audit traceability across incidents.
